searchText: I have a question: cryptography is great to prove that "I have done something". Is there a way to prove "I have done something before this given timestamp"? Even with a controlled error margin it'd be useful Yes, use a blockchain. Blockchains are *really good* at proving timestamps of things. well, I want to use this so that a block proposer needs to prove that it submitted the block before a given timestamp, so relying on a blockchain doesn't work 1. Create a file. 2. Hash the file. 3. Write the hash of the file to Ethereum block 12345. 4. Sometime later, reveal the file and point at the hash written at block 12345 to prove that you created the file prior to that block. Oh, you can't do this. oh, so there's a theorem like this? This is a well known problem because you have a problem of not being able to identify whether the payload was sent and not received or not sent at all. Byzantine Generals problem. Thanks for the keywords!

2. Hash the file.
3. Write the hash of the file to Ethereum block 12345.
4. Sometime later, reveal the file and point at the hash written at block 12345 to prove that you created the file prior to that block.
